call_points.text: Total new orders year-to-date 9 months reached INR9.7 billion in India and approximately INR3 billion in Europe.
A new American iron castings programme adds about ₹200 Cr a year and fills existing foundry capacity, requiring a new line.
H1 CY26 capex was ₹210 Cr versus ₹380 Cr for full CY25; H2 capex is expected to be significantly higher.
Expansions under way in gears at Rajkot and Chakan, composites, stampings at Pune, and forgings at Chakan and Bengaluru.
Two or three greenfield projects are in late-stage customer negotiation but not yet approved.
India margin fell 80 bps on West Asia-driven cost inflation; most is expected to be recouped in the next two quarters.
Net financial debt was negative ₹1,420 Cr, leaving the company in net cash for organic and inorganic growth.
Mexico revenue fell about 20% as a customer in-sourced production and renegotiated the contract over more years.
Analysts pressed on seven to eight quarters of underperformance and thin disclosure; management acknowledged the concern but gave no new granularity.
Inorganic growth is constrained by high Indian valuation expectations; management says business cases are not positive.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Background This Case relates to erstwhile Mahindra Ugine Steel Company Limited (“MUSCO”) which merged with the Company pursuant to Integrated Scheme of Amalgamation. The Assessing officer had passed an Assessment Order for AY 2005-06 on account of Certain disallowances and accordingly had raised a demand notice vide an Order dated November 11, 2007. The Company, being aggrieved with the said Order issued by Assessing Officer filed appeal before the Hon’ble Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)]. The Hon’ble CIT(A) in its Order partially upheld the Company’s claim. Both the parties i.e. Income tax department & the Company being aggrieved by the said Order issued by the Hon’ble CIT(A) filed cross appeals before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT). The Honourable ITAT in view of the contentions made by both the parties after its due consideration remanded the case to CIT(A) for fresh adjudication on November 16, 2018. Status update upto Last Quarter CIT(A) vide its order dated 18th September 2025 has partially allowed the appeal filed by the Company. While the deduction claimed by the Company to the extent of INR 132 Million were allowed, the deduction claimed to the extent of INR 134 Million were dis-allowed. The Company has view that the case of the Company is strong in relation to the said dis-allowed deductions and hence a further appeal shall be filed by the Company against the said order.
tax_litigation.status: During the quarter under review the Company has filed an appeal before the honourable Income tax appellate tribunal, Mumbai against the dis-allowed deduction of INR 134 Million. As per the Legal Opinion, the Company have good case on merits to defend this liability. Total expected financial impact in case this further appeal can be upto INR 45 Million. The same is not material for the Company. Accordingly, the present appeal filed by the Company no longer remains a material litigation for the Company in accordance with Sub para 8 of part B of Schedule III of SEBI LODR.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Background:- During the processing of return of income for AY 2020-2021, Central Processing Unit (“CPC”) erred in considering certain operating revenue twice and also made disallowances erroneously and certain advance payments of tax were missed to be considered. Intimation u/s 143(1) was issued by CPC on October 29, 2021 against which an application was filed by the company, for rectification u/s 154 with the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer (“AO”) and with the Faceless AO simultaneously by the Company. Dispute details:- An application has been filed with the Assessing Officer against the erroneous adjustments made by CPC during processing of the Company’s Income Tax return on various grounds like erroneous additions of item of incomes twice, disallowance of certain amount as expense, short grant of tax deducted at source and levying consequential interest thereon. This resulted in raising of tax demand of Rs. 32,97,47,360/- as against the refund claimed by the Company of Rs. 20,98,00,000/-. Thereafter, the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax has forwarded Order of assessment in the application as mentioned above filed with the Assessing Officer against the erroneous adjustments made by CPC during processing of the Company’s Income Tax return is accepted in favour of the Company. The demand of Income Tax of INR 32,97,47,360/- as per the CPC Assessment is converted into a refund of INR 14,52,16,939/- as per the Assessment under Section 143(3) read with Section 144C(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Hence, the proceedings before the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax relating to said matter stands concluded. However, the said refund is below the refund claimed by the Company of INR 20,98,00,000/-. Hence, the company filed appeal in December 2023 before CIT (Appeals) to claim the deficit in refund of INR 64,583,061/-.
tax_litigation.status: No update in current quarter. The appeal for refund continues to be pending before CIT Appeals.

operating_notes.text: India segment sales ₹1,663.5 Cr in Q1CY26 with segment profit before tax and interest of ₹230.2 Cr; Europe sales ₹948.5 Cr with ₹108.2 Cr.
Europe sales rose 17% YoY including a +17% exchange-rate impact, with volumes in line with a light-vehicle market down 1.4%.
India market volumes in Q1CY26: light vehicles 1.75 mn (+9.4% YoY), two-wheelers 7.06 mn (+20.7%), tractors 0.34 mn (+37.3%), MHCVs 149.4 thousand (+24.9%).
CIE Automotive India secured ₹350 crore per year in new orders during Q1 CY26, with 11% from EVs.
Suryadeep GJ3 Project Private Limited, a 26.09% associate from 15 May 2026, will set up a captive solar plant of around 1.6 MWp to supply power to CIE Automotive's Rajkot, Gujarat factories.
New order book of about ₹500 Cr a year won in H1 CY26, spread across verticals.
The American iron castings programme adds about ₹200 Cr a year of turnover; dispatches have started but revenue recognition begins next quarter.
Gears grew 18%, composites 17% and stampings 16% in Q2 CY26.
Q2FY27 India segment revenue ₹1,852 Cr (+18% YoY) versus Europe ₹781 Cr (-15% QoQ).
Q2FY27 other income ₹43.90 Cr, up 129% YoY, lifted pre-tax profit.
Q3CY26 India segment revenue grew 18% YoY to ₹1,852.14 Cr while Europe segment revenue declined 3% YoY to ₹781.28 Cr.
India Q3 CY26 sales at INR18 billion (+18% YoY); Europe Q3 CY26 sales at INR7.6 billion (-4% YoY).
